cut_items.item: Auditing/CVE response: can't tell which base image a deployment was built from
Caching pitfall: stale local 'latest' vs newer pull on clean CI runner causes inconsistent builds
Upgrades surface as CI/prod failures in unrelated commits, with concrete examples (Python 3.12 to 3.13, bookworm to trixie)
Even for dev, pinned tag is a good habit
Auditing and CVE response: you can't say which base image a deployment was built from
Cache inconsistency: a stale local :latest can differ from what a clean CI runner pulls
Concrete breaking-change examples: Python 3.12 to 3.13, Debian bookworm to trixie
The tag stays alongside the digest for readability while the digest guarantees the exact bytes
Even in dev, a pinned tag is a good habit

added_items.item: Supply-chain risk: bad or compromised upstream push reaches production builds without review
Command to get digest: docker buildx imagetools inspect <image:tag>
Caveat: pinning a digest stops automatic patches, so the update bot is needed to stay current
Rollbacks unreliable: rebuilding an old commit doesn't give the old image
:latest doesn't necessarily mean newest or most stable; maintainer decides
Command to get the digest: docker buildx imagetools inspect <image:tag>
Rollback risk: rebuilding an old commit doesn't give back the old image
Supply-chain risk: a bad or compromised upstream push reaches production builds unreviewed

Pinning a digest stops automatic patches, so the update bot is what keeps you current
